title: @ankhorage/types
summary: Publishes reusable TypeScript declarations through explicit package subpaths for independently released applications.
purpose: Give independently released applications a portable package of shared TypeScript declarations, including feature-specific contracts such as ZORA types.
responsibilities: Publish reusable TypeScript declarations through intentional public package entrypoints.
Group related declarations by owner and expose feature-specific types through explicit subpaths such as @ankhorage/types/zora.
Keep shared type contracts portable for independent consumers.
boundaries: Does not implement application workflows, UI components, runtime behavior, persistence, deployment, or infrastructure operations.
Does not replace feature-owning packages or execute application capabilities.
Does not require consumers to use an Ankhorage application, repository, or unpublished sibling source.
audience: TypeScript application authors who need shared Ankhorage declarations without importing feature implementations.
Maintainers integrating feature-specific contracts, such as ZORA provider types, into independent applications.
useCases: Import shared declarations from the package root or an explicit feature subpath.
Use ZORA contracts through imports such as import { type ZoraProvider } from '@ankhorage/types/zora'.
Share compile-time contracts between independently released applications and feature packages.

architecture.role: Portable TypeScript declaration library with topic-owned contracts and explicit public package subpaths.
invariants: Consumers use published package entrypoints and declared dependencies rather than sibling source imports.
Declarations remain portable and do not require feature implementations, platform frameworks, or provider SDKs at runtime.
Each feature-specific contract is exposed through its intentional public subpath.

limitations: Declarations describe compile-time contracts only and do not provide runtime implementations.
Consumers must use the matching feature package when they need the behavior represented by a declaration.
